A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DACA research work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and matchable. V2 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: V1 reports original calibration experiments on multiple-choice and open-ended QA, including comparisons across models, calibration methods, and post-training strategies.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and their numerical results in the main text and Appendix E.

M1.justification: DACA retains the same agreement-filtered KL objective, temperature optimization, and vector/matrix-scaling extensions. V1 Equation (6) becomes v2 Equation (7). The added confidence formula explains the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MMLU, MedMCQA, MathQA, and TruthfulQA, retaining the same multiple-choice, open-ended QA, and selective-classification coverage. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged within the corresponding experiments, including CAPE, Elicitation, Elicitation-Ensemble, and supervised scaling methods. Elicitation-Ensemble receives a different citation, but its aggregation description and evaluated entries remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics, model configurations, prompts, and splits remain unchanged. Appendix D retains Adam, batch size 256, learning rate 0.05, 400 calibration epochs, subject-specific MMLU validation sets, and the 7:3 test-to-validation ratio elsewhere.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same analyses of naive alignment, model size, PLM choice, post-training strategies, scaling extensions, and selective classification. The corresponding figures and supplementary analyses supply no new evidence in v2.

E5.justification: The new checklist, item 7, describes results as means and standard errors. Appendix D in both versions instead specifies standard deviations over five prompts or five random splits. This introduces a conflicting uncertainty description without documenting changed runs or recalculated error bars.

E6.justification: Matched result entries, rankings, and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains Gemma-3-12B-Instruct's DACA ECE of 8.596%, and Table 2 retains GPT-4o's 6.993% ECE using Gemma-3-12B. Appendix E's results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Propositions 3.2–3.3, and Appendix C's proofs are unchanged. V2 Equation (1) explicitly writes the existing softmax probabilities and maximum-probability confidence; it adds explanation rather than a new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty and effectiveness claims for unsupervised agreement-based calibration, including applicability to API models, open-ended QA, and selective classification. Minor wording changes do not alter their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of disagreement-induced under-confidence and selective-classification benefits remain unchanged. The limitations still concern additional PLM inference cost and loss of calibration examples through filtering. The checklist adds no substantive new limitation.

D1.justification: V2 adds a public-code statement and repository address in the introduction, plus code-release statements in the checklist. Section 2.1 explicitly documents choice-logit normalization. Appendix D's implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4.1 changes Elicitation-Ensemble's attribution from Tie et al.'s post-training survey to Xiong et al. (2023a), a confidence-elicitation study. Appendix A adds Tao et al. (2025) and mentions numerical and linguistic verbalized confidence. The main research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 expands Section 2.1, makes localized grammar edits, updates the conference footer, and appends a 16-item NeurIPS checklist. The main narrative and organization of Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–E remain intact.

P2.justification: All eight figures and twelve tables are retained with the same substantive displays. Figure 3 moves from page 7 to page 8, Table 3 from page 8 to page 9, and surrounding text reflows. The checklist adds a separate formatted section.

improvement.justification: V2 provides modest gains in clarity and reproducibility documentation through explicit MCQA confidence notation, a code-access pointer, and better-targeted baseline attribution. The scientific evidence remains unchanged. The new checklist's standard-error statement conflicts with Appendix D's standard-deviation description, a reporting drawback that limits the overall improvement.
